pairs.subject: time-travel-replay
pairs.evidence: src/hooks/execution/useReplayTimeline.ts:83 gives every log line an evenly-apportioned timestamp instead of its recorded one, so dead air is smeared away, no gap can render as disclosed silence, and the whole playback asserts a tempo the record never contained.

techniques.evidence: src/hooks/execution/useReplayTimeline.ts:83 computes timestamp_ms as (index / (n-1)) * totalMs — every line's position is invented by apportionment, which is the technique's named interpolation failure; the measured tool-step stream (real started_at_ms) and the fabricated line stream then share one axis with no stated time authority, and a gap can never exist to be disclosed.

src/hooks/execution/useReplayTimeline.ts:156-165 computes accumulatedCost as (completed-step fraction + active-step fraction) x the settled total rather than a prefix sum over cost records, so the end-state reconciliation invariant holds by construction and can never surface a disagreement between the replay fold and the rollup — the cross-check the technique exists to provide is structurally unreachable.

src/features/agents/sub_executions/replay/ReplayTerminalPanel.tsx:109 is a second, replay-only renderer of the same log-line vocabulary the live surface renders in src/features/shared/components/terminal/TerminalBody.tsx:42, and the two have already diverged: JSON pretty-printing exists only in replay (ReplayTerminalPanel.tsx:9-89) while virtualization, filtering and summary lines exist only live — so a replay frame cannot be indistinguishable from the live frame it imitates, and 'replay looks wrong' has no single defect behind it.

The cost half is exemplary — ReplayCostPanel.tsx:41-46 prefixes '~' with the reason recorded, CostAccrualOverlay.tsx:95-107 dashes the curve unconditionally and distinguishes two different estimate facts, PipelineWaterfall.tsx:103-110 badges a synthetic trace — but the apportioned line timings (useReplayTimeline.ts:16,:83) are marked nowhere, and ReplaySandbox.tsx:134-160 opens straight into the transport with no idle-state provenance or coverage disclosure, so the viewer consents to the fiction without learning its genre.

TimelineScrubber.tsx:160-161 shows only elapsed/total offsets with no gap markers or compressed regions (dead-air compression cannot exist once the timeline is apportioned), and useReplayTimeline.ts:215 makes jumpToStart force-pause, so the gesture toggles intent rather than only moving the viewpoint. Correct parts: scrubTo leaves isPlaying alone (:208), speed is an exchange rate applied forward (:177), and 'ended' leaves the run scrubbable (:194-196).

src/hooks/execution/useReplayTimeline.ts:88-97 finds the visible-line cutoff by binary search rather than folding at render time, :99-100 and :179-184 throttle playback flushes to ~12/s so derived lists do not recompute at 60fps, ReplayTerminalPanel.tsx:97-106 memoizes per-line classification and highlighting, and every cache is memo-scoped so it dies with the replay session.

pairs.registryProposal: timeline-derivation names a stated failure for records too damaged to parse, but not for the far commoner case this repo is in: a record that parses perfectly and simply contains no per-item timing (here, a log blob plus a duration and a total cost). That record cannot support a timeline, yet the honest-looking move — apportion and play — is exactly what shipped, and it defeats gap disclosure, dead-air compression and the accrual reconciliation invariant all at once, silently. Worth a third outcome alongside 'built' and 'could not build': 'the record does not support a timeline; offer the settled view instead', with apportionment named as the failure mode it is.

pairs.registryProposal: Upward lesson for consolidation's 'the measure follows the question' section: the standard frames the min-normalized (directional) measure as belonging to duplicate-and-correction detection, but memoryConflicts.ts:121-124,143 found a sharper split — min-normalized topic overlap drives contradiction and supersedence while union-normalized similarity drives duplicate — and, more importantly, that CHECK ORDER is load-bearing in a way the standard does not state: every negation pair is a one-word swap ('always'/'never'), so a genuine contradiction scores above the duplicate threshold and, if the duplicate branch runs first, the sharpest contradictions in the store are the ones guaranteed to be mislabelled and offered a Merge button. Worth adding to the technique as 'check contradiction before duplicate' with this repo's file:line as the field evidence.
